claims.title: Supplier compliance documents may be intercepted on the unverified public-to-vendor portal path
claims.description: `flow:entity:supplier>process:supplier-portal>upload-documents` crosses from `boundary:public-internet` to `boundary:vendor-platform` and carries supplier staff contact details and compliance paperwork. Its `encryption_in_transit` and protocol are unknown. If transport protection is absent or ineffective, an attacker able to observe this crossing can intercept the documents and PII in transit. The disclosed documents can then be used to profile suppliers and their staff for targeted fraud or social engineering against the portal.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:supplier>process:supplier-portal>upload-documents` crosses the public-internet-to-vendor-platform boundary while its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. Impact is medium because the flow carries PII and business-critical compliance documents.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encrypted portal transport
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ for `flow:entity:supplier>process:supplier-portal>upload-documents`, verify certificate validation and modern cipher configuration, and record the resulting protocol and `encryption_in_transit` attributes.

mitigations.summary: Minimize sensitive document content in requests
mitigations.detail: Where practical, transmit opaque upload references after a protected upload session rather than exposing unnecessary supplier identifiers in request metadata.

claims.title: Category-manager document reviews may be intercepted across the corporate-to-vendor boundary
claims.description: `flow:entity:category-manager>process:supplier-portal>review-documents` crosses from `boundary:corporate-network` into `boundary:vendor-platform`; its authentication, protocol, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the review connection lacks effective transport encryption, a network observer can intercept document-review content, approvals, and rejections, exposing supplier-related business decisions and any PII returned during review. That information enables targeted impersonation or manipulation attempts against category managers and suppliers.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the review flow crosses from `boundary:corporate-network` to `boundary:vendor-platform` with unverified protocol and `encryption_in_transit`. Impact is medium because the flow handles PII and business-critical review and approval information.

mitigations.summary: Require authenticated TLS for manager review sessions
mitigations.detail: Enforce TLS 1.2+ with valid certificate verification for `flow:entity:category-manager>process:supplier-portal>review-documents`, and document the authentication mechanism used by category managers.

mitigations.summary: Reduce sensitive response fields
mitigations.detail: Return only the document and approval fields needed for a manager's current review, avoiding unnecessary staff-contact or document metadata in responses.

claims.title: Uploaded documents may be readable on the unverified portal-to-document-store path
claims.description: `flow:process:supplier-portal>store:document-store>store-documents` transfers uploaded compliance documents between `process:supplier-portal` and `store:document-store`, but its protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If this vendor-internal path is unencrypted, an attacker able to observe the path can intercept supplier paperwork and staff PII while it is stored. The documents can reveal supplier operations and contacts useful for subsequent targeting of the vendor portal or supplier organizations.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because intercepting this intra-vendor-platform path requires a network or infrastructure foothold, although its protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unverified. Impact is medium because the flow carries PII and business-critical compliance documents.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the portal-to-store hop
mitigations.detail: Require TLS, preferably mutually authenticated TLS where supported, for `flow:process:supplier-portal>store:document-store>store-documents` and obtain vendor evidence of the control.

mitigations.summary: Constrain document-store access
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated portal identity with only the write and object-prefix permissions required for document ingestion.

claims.title: Nightly supplier extract may be intercepted between the vendor and landing bucket
claims.description: `flow:entity:portal-vendor>store:landing-bucket>push-nightly-extract` crosses from `boundary:vendor-platform` to `boundary:cloud-account` and carries the nightly supplier data extract. Its protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the channel is not effectively encrypted, an on-path attacker can intercept the extract containing supplier PII and business-critical records before it reaches `store:landing-bucket`. The raw extract can enable broad profiling of suppliers and their staff and provides data useful for attacks on downstream supplier-record processing. The source's statement that the file arrives as a plain CSV does not establish whether its transport channel was encrypted, so this remains conditional.

quotes.text: The runbook for the landing bucket says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because this is a vendor-platform-to-cloud-account boundary crossing with unknown protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit`. Impact is medium because the nightly extract carries PII and business-critical supplier records in bulk.

mitigations.summary: Require a mutually authenticated encrypted delivery channel
mitigations.detail: Use TLS 1.2+ with vendor client authentication, or a managed private-transfer mechanism, for `flow:entity:portal-vendor>store:landing-bucket>push-nightly-extract` and verify it in the landing-bucket runbook.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the extract independently of transport
mitigations.detail: Require the vendor to encrypt each extract file before delivery using a customer-controlled recipient key, so a captured transfer does not reveal the records.

claims.title: Supplier master service may receive the extract over an unverified bucket read path
claims.description: `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract` reads the nightly supplier extract from `store:landing-bucket`, but its protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the service-to-bucket read path lacks effective encryption, an attacker with a foothold on that path can intercept the raw CSV extract as it is loaded. The captured PII and supplier records can then be correlated with records written to `store:supplier-database` for further targeted attacks.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because observing the cloud-account-internal read path requires a prior foothold, although protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. Impact is medium because the read transfers a nightly extract containing PII and business-critical supplier data.

mitigations.summary: Require encrypted authenticated bucket reads
mitigations.detail: Configure `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract` to use the cloud provider's TLS-protected endpoint with workload identity authentication, and record the verified settings.

mitigations.summary: Limit extract exposure duration
mitigations.detail: Use a narrowly scoped, short-lived service identity and remove or archive the extract immediately after successful processing under controls appropriate to its PII content.

claims.title: Supplier records may be intercepted on the unverified service-to-database write path
claims.description: `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:supplier-database>write-supplier-records` writes supplier records to `store:supplier-database`, while its protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the database connection is not encrypted, an attacker able to observe the cloud-account path can intercept supplier PII and business-critical record content in transit. The exposed records can be used to identify and target suppliers and staff represented in the downstream database.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because an attacker needs a foothold on the internal cloud-account path, while protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` remain unverified. Impact is medium because supplier records contain PII and business-critical data.

mitigations.summary: Enforce TLS for database writes
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ with certificate validation for `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:supplier-database>write-supplier-records` and reject non-TLS database connections.

mitigations.summary: Use a dedicated workload database identity
mitigations.detail: Authenticate the supplier master service with a narrowly scoped workload identity rather than a reusable broad database credential.

claims.title: Vendor document-store copies may expose supplier documents if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:document-store` holds uploaded compliance documents with PII and business-critical content, but its data classification and `encryption_at_rest` are unknown. If the unknown encryption setting resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains a storage-layer copy, such as retained media or an operational copy within the vendor platform, can read the documents without using the portal access path. The disclosure enables supplier and staff profiling and targeted follow-on attacks. This is conditional on `encryption_at_rest`; it does not assert that the vendor store is unencrypted.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the attacker must obtain a storage-layer copy and `store:document-store` may in fact be encrypted at rest. Impact is medium because the store contains PII and business-critical compliance documents.

mitigations.summary: Verify vendor encryption at rest and coverage of operational copies
mitigations.detail: Obtain evidence that `store:document-store` uses encryption at rest and that backups, snapshots, replicas, and media-decommissioning processes are covered by the same protection.

mitigations.summary: Restrict vendor storage and key access
mitigations.detail: Require least-privilege storage access and documented key-custody controls so staff or systems handling operational copies cannot read document contents unnecessarily.

claims.title: A storage-layer copy of the landing bucket may disclose the nightly supplier extract
claims.description: `store:landing-bucket` holds the nightly supplier data extract, including PII and business-critical data, but its data classification and `encryption_at_rest` are unknown. If encryption at rest is absent, an attacker holding a copied bucket object, backup, or underlying storage artifact can read the raw extract without authenticating through `process:supplier-master-service`. The extract can then be used to profile the supplier population and to target records subsequently loaded into `store:supplier-database`. This is a conditional storage-copy threat, not an assertion that the bucket is unencrypted.

quotes.text: The runbook for the landing bucket says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because an attacker must acquire a storage-layer copy and `store:landing-bucket` has unverified rather than absent encryption at rest. Impact is medium because the bucket holds a bulk supplier extract containing PII and business-critical data.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the landing bucket and every retained copy
mitigations.detail: Require encryption at rest for `store:landing-bucket` using managed customer-controlled keys where available, explicitly covering versioned objects, backups, snapshots, and exports.

mitigations.summary: Reduce retention of raw extracts
mitigations.detail: Delete or securely archive the raw extract promptly after validation and loading, with access controls at least as strict as those for the supplier database.

claims.title: A storage-layer copy of the supplier database may disclose supplier records
claims.description: `store:supplier-database` contains supplier records tagged as PII and business-critical data, while its data classification and `encryption_at_rest` are unknown. If the database is not encrypted at rest, an attacker who obtains a database volume, backup, snapshot, or decommissioned-storage copy can read the supplier corpus directly without going through application authorization. The disclosed records can be used for broad supplier and staff profiling and enable targeted attacks against downstream business relationships. This threat is conditional on the unresolved `encryption_at_rest` attribute.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because obtaining a database storage copy is an additional prerequisite and `store:supplier-database` may be encrypted at rest. Impact is medium because the database holds PII and business-critical supplier records.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce database encryption at rest
mitigations.detail: Establish the encryption posture of `store:supplier-database` and require encryption at rest with managed keys for database storage, backups, snapshots, and replicas.

mitigations.summary: Control backup and key access separately
mitigations.detail: Restrict export, snapshot, restore, and key-use permissions to separate least-privileged roles, and audit access to stored database copies.

claims.title: Code running in the supplier master service may read the raw landing-bucket extract through its unverified access path
claims.description: `process:supplier-master-service` reads the raw nightly extract from `store:landing-bucket` through `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract`, whose authentication is unknown. If the service's bucket grant permits broad object reads, an attacker running code in the service can use that existing access path to read the extract and disclose supplier PII and business-critical data. The raw data then reaches the supplier-record pipeline represented by `store:supplier-database`, increasing the value of the disclosure. This draft is conditional on the unresolved authentication and authorization scope; it does not claim that the service is already compromised or that its grant is over-broad.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the attacker must first run code in `process:supplier-master-service`, and the authentication and resulting access scope on `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract` are unknown. Impact is medium because the landing bucket holds a PII-bearing, business-critical nightly supplier extract.

mitigations.summary: Scope the service identity to the single expected extract
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated workload identity for `process:supplier-master-service` that can read only the expected object prefix and only for the time needed to process each nightly extract.

mitigations.summary: Make raw-extract reads auditable
mitigations.detail: Log bucket object reads by the supplier master service and alert on unexpected object names, volumes, source contexts, or access outside the scheduled load window.
